clips.title: The story
paras: Dangers of the Windfury is a rite of martial readiness offered by Ruul Eagletalon in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren and Horde adventurers are tasked with battling the savage Windfury harpies nesting in the southeastern cliffs of Mulgore. Hunting these feral predators serves as an essential test of skill and survival before journeying beyond the tribal homeland.

In Bloodhoof Village, the veteran warrior Ruul Eagletalon observes all travelers who pass through the heart of Mulgore. For those coming of age or seeking to prove themselves ready for wider adventures, Ruul demands tangible proof of their combat instincts. Survival beyond the sheltered valleys of Mulgore requires poise against aggressive, cunning foes, and Ruul uses the land's fiercest native predators to measure a youth's mettle.

The Windfury harpies roost along the mountainous southeastern rim of Mulgore, safely off the beaten trails but constantly posing a threat to wandering wildlife and isolated travelers. Vicious and relentlessly hungry for fresh flesh, these avian terrors rely on swift swoops and razor-sharp claws. Defeating them and claiming their talons demonstrates not only the power to defeat an entrenched threat, but the speed required to counter aerial raiders.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Thank you for taking the time to speak to me, friend. I am Ruul, warrior and teacher.
You have obviously reached an age when you must prepare for your trials if you are to adventure much further out of Mulgore.
If you wish a test of your strength, start by seeking out the Windfury harpies to the southeast. They nestle along the mountain's edges away from the road.
They are one of our natural enemies here in Mulgore and will be a good gauge of your skill.

clips.title: Progress
paras: The Windfuries are deadly foes. Their strength in battle is only rivaled by their desire for fresh meat.

clips.title: Completion
paras: You have done well, friend. You seem well prepared to travel onward. Let the wind always be at your back.
